advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test case that passes an arm64 generating `binary_sha256` in the provenance dict to cover the widened generating-binary acceptance path.
evidence: "binary_sha256": fingerprints["darwin-arm64"],  # provenance generating hash fixed to intel value across all iterations
The for-loop varies only the `binary_sha256=` kwarg (installed), not the provenance generating `binary_sha256`.
advisory.finding: The new test varies only the installed `binary_sha256` argument across both darwin-arm64 hashes; the generating-binary membership check (which was also widened to accept both hashes at line 148) is exercised only with the intel hash held fixed in the provenance's `binary_sha256`, so acceptance of the arm64 hash on the generating path is never asserted.
scenarios: A regression that narrowed the generating-path accepted set to reject the arm64 hash would not be caught by this test.

advisory.finding: The newly-added generating-binary membership check (accepted_generating = ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256[str(generating_platform)]; 'if generating_hash not in accepted_generating') is never exercised with the widened arm64 fingerprint. Every test sets provenance['binary_sha256'] (the generating hash, per line 140) to fingerprints['darwin-arm64'] = the Intel hash, so the arm64 acceptance on the generating path and its new 'expected one of ...' error message are untested.

advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize or extend the new test so provenance['binary_sha256'] takes _ARM64_DARWIN (accept) and 'f'*64 (reject, asserting 'Pandoc generating binary SHA-256 mismatch' and both accepted hashes in the message).
